_README: Keys are '<CODE>:<Symbol>' exactly as scripts/check_app_wiring.py prints them. The value is why the finding is accepted, and it should name the issue that will make it stop firing. Checked in BOTH directions: an entry whose finding no longer fires fails the run, so this file cannot rot into a list of things that used to be true. Delete an entry the moment its page lands.
_WHY_THIS_FILE_IS_LONG_TODAY: Every entry below is the same fact said twenty-five times: app/ is a skeleton whose ViewModels exist and whose Views do not, so every command and every observable property is genuinely bound to nothing. That is not a false positive; it is the guard correctly describing an unfinished app. Each entry names the issue whose page will bind it, and the entry must be deleted in that issue's own PR.
UNBOUND-DISPLAY-PROPERTY:RunTargetOption: #568: not shown by its own row; RunTargetPickerViewModel copies it into the picker's Note (RunTargetPickerViewModel.cs:147,186,222), which the page binds. Stays unbound by construction.
UNBOUND-DISPLAY-PROPERTY:SetupStepRow.Re: #568: the copy-to-clipboard text for the 'ask your admin' button (SetupStepsViewModel.cs:235, WizardViewModel.cs:365); it is never displayed on screen, by design.
CODE-ONLY-COMMAND:NewRunViewModel.AddDro: #63, done: Drop is an event, not a bindable Command= property, so NewRunPage.xaml.cs forwards the dropped items to this command (the same shape as NavigateToCommand). Stays C#-only by construction.
CODE-ONLY-COMMAND:NewRunViewModel.Receiv: #108, done: the navigation parameter is not bindable from XAML, so NewRunPage.xaml.cs forwards it from OnNavigatedTo in one call (the same shape as AddDroppedCommand). Stays C#-only by construction.
TEST-ONLY-COMMAND:WizardViewModel.Choose: #99, done: the wizard page binds each project in the list to ProjectChoice.ChooseCommand (WizardPage.xaml), which calls this command inside WizardViewModel.cs. The guard only counts references outside the declaring file, so it still reads TEST-ONLY by name; the entry is not stale (MEASURED 2026-10-15: removing it fails check_app_wiring.py).
CODE-ONLY-OBSERVABLE:WizardViewModel.Sel: #99 builds the first-run wizard pages; the CODE-ONLY classification is a name collision with IGcpAccount.SelectedProjectId (read by JobEngine and ShellViewModel), see the script docstring on name matching.
CODE-ONLY-OBSERVABLE:RunProgressViewMode: #66; the CODE-ONLY classification is a name collision with IRunRepository.JobId, see the script's docstring on name matching
TEST-ONLY-OBSERVABLE:RunProgressViewMode: #66, done: CanCancel only ever drives CancelCommand's CanExecute via [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor]; WinUI's Button.Command already syncs IsEnabled from ICommand.CanExecuteChanged, so no view ever needs to read the bool property itself.
#66, done: same reasoning as CanCancel above, for StopVmCommand/DeleteVmCommand.

#66, done: RunProgressPage binds the derived StageTitle text, not the raw JobPhase enum; a future accessibility pass (docs/ui_conventions.md section 5's LiveSetting=Polite) may bind CurrentPhase directly for Narrator, which would clear this entry.
